video_title: Eddie Johnson, Draymond Green Social Media BEEF, Stephen A. Smith Said What? | Edification Episode 3

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith praises the Lakers' recent performance and coaching
quotes.excerpt: I'm saying LA doing special things. The Lakers are doing special things.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: I'm looking at the brothers, and I'm saying LA doing special things. The Lakers are doing special things. JJ Redick right now, as far as I'm concerned, is one of the leading candidates for Coach of the Year. Rob Pelinka and what he's put together might be an Executive of the Year with the way he's doing the job. Hell of a job. Luka Doncic is just all-world. Austin Reaves is showing you how he can ball. Kaka Walker, I mean, this brother can play. I got it.

text_blocks.speaker: Justin Termine
text_blocks.text: Damn, I'm so glad you said it, because they can't. Well, I'm going to say it for them. I'm going to go, I'm looking at the fellas. Yeah, yeah. LA looked pretty damn good.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson clarifies his stance on Stephen A. Smith's comments
quotes.excerpt: I'm not interested in calling Stephen A. Smith racist. I don't know what's in his heart.
quotes.quote: I'm not interested in calling Stephen A. Smith racist. I don't know what's in his heart, and I don't believe we should automatically reach for that label every time somebody makes a statement involving race. I want to go deeper. I just want to examine the thinking, because sometimes people repeat assumptions without ever questioning where those assumptions came from.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson discusses Tiger Woods' impact on golf's history
quotes.excerpt: Tiger Woods one of the greatest athletes I've ever witnessed. But to appreciate what Tiger accomplished,
quotes.quote: Tiger Woods one of the greatest athletes I've ever witnessed. But to appreciate what Tiger accomplished, you have to understand the history of golf. Did you know the PGA of America maintained a Caucasian-only membership rule until 1961? Think about that. You could have talent, discipline, determination, but your opportunity could be limited because of your skin color. That's not competition, that's controlling who gets to compete.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson highlights Jackie Robinson breaking baseball's color barrier
quotes.excerpt: Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball's modern color barrier in 1947. He wasn't just competing against pitchers,
quotes.quote: Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball's modern color barrier in 1947. He wasn't just competing against pitchers, he was competing against racial hostility, against exclusion, against people who believed he didn't belong. But Jackie Robinson, he could play baseball, couldn't he? And once those barriers began coming down, the game gained access to extraordinary talent.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson on the impact of Dominican players in baseball
quotes.excerpt: Look at the influence Dominican players have had on baseball. Pedro Martinez, David Ortiz, Albert Pujols, Vladimir Guerrero.
quotes.quote: Look at the influence Dominican players have had on baseball. Pedro Martinez, David Ortiz, Albert Pujols, Vladimir Guerrero. Different histories, different journeys, but the same lesson. Talent doesn't belong to one group. And imagine how much greatness was lost when people weren't given the opportunity to compete.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson discusses Willie O'Ree breaking the NHL color barrier
quotes.excerpt: Willie O'Ree broke the NHL color barrier in 1958. Black players have faced obstacles involving access,
quotes.quote: Willie O'Ree broke the NHL color barrier in 1958. Black players have faced obstacles involving access, development opportunities, and racial hostility. And hockey is an expensive sport, like tennis. So here's the problem. If a group has limited access to a sport, and then people use that group's low participation as proof they aren't capable, they've actually confused lack of opportunity with lack of ability. And those are two completely different things.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson discusses Caitlin Clark's impact on the WNBA
quotes.excerpt: Caitlin Clark. Her arrival brought enormous attention to the WNBA. Television audiences, ticket sales, media coverage, corporate interests.
quotes.quote: Caitlin Clark. Her arrival brought enormous attention to the WNBA. Television audiences, ticket sales, media coverage, corporate interests. But the league already had outstanding players. They had champions, they had MVPs, women who helped actually build that league long before Caitlin Clark arrived. And many had not received the recognition they deserved. So when Clark arrived and received extraordinary attention, it raised complicated questions about recognition, race, and media coverage.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson reflects on his NBA career and competition
quotes.excerpt: I played professional basketball for 18 years. Competed against Magic Johnson, Larry Bird, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, and Michael Jordan.
quotes.quote: I played professional basketball for 18 years. Competed against Magic Johnson, Larry Bird, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, and Michael Jordan. And some of the greatest players in NBA history. And I can tell you something, when I stepped on that court, I wasn't worried about what somebody looked like. I wasn't worried about whether I could stop a particular player. Larry Bird was probably one of the toughest competitors I've ever faced. And if you were worried about his skin color instead of his basketball ability, you were about to have a very long night.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson responds to claims about the Lakers' championship chances
quotes.excerpt: If you're going to tell me the Los Angeles Lakers cannot win an NBA championship, give me
quotes.quote: If you're going to tell me the Los Angeles Lakers cannot win an NBA championship, give me basketball reasons. Tell me they don't defend well. Tell me they lack depth. Tell me their roster creates matchup problems. Tell me their opponents are just better. I can respect those arguments. It's between the lines. See, we can debate those things all day long. But if the racial identity of three players becomes the central reason why they're supposedly cannot win a championship, then you've changed the conversation.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson shares his experience at the University of Illinois
quotes.excerpt: I grew up in Chicago, inner city, Cabrini-Green, North Side of Chicago. I was raised by a single
quotes.quote: I grew up in Chicago, inner city, Cabrini-Green, North Side of Chicago. I was raised by a single mother in a family of seven. And I understood early that opportunities weren't always equal. But I also learned something about competing. You don't allow somebody else's expectations to determine your ceiling. You prepare, you work, you compete, and when the opportunity comes, you make the most of it. I went to the University of Illinois, and I experienced something at Illinois that I thought would push me back, but I was very competitive.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson on his freshman year at Illinois and Lou Henson
quotes.excerpt: My first year, Lou Henson did not play me. I knew why. I wasn't strong enough yet.
quotes.quote: My first year, Lou Henson did not play me. I knew why. I wasn't strong enough yet. I was 185 pounds when I stepped foot on Illinois' campus. And Lou Henson told me, he said, Eddie, you can shoot the ball better than anybody in the country, but it's hard to shoot when you're laying on your back. Basically what he told me is I wasn't strong enough to compete in the Big Ten at that moment.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson on missing a test and his coach's reaction
quotes.excerpt: We won a trip, and I had an excuse to miss a test. Came back, I approached the
quotes.quote: We won a trip, and I had an excuse to miss a test. Came back, I approached the TA, and I said, here's my excuse. I need to take the test that you gave on Friday. It happened to be a Monday that I asked him that. He looked at me, and he said, you need to get your priorities in order. I'm not going to allow you to take the test over. I said, I have an excuse, a university excuse. And he then said, I don't care. And I said, well, you will care because I am going to take the test.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson on his academic struggle and determination
quotes.excerpt: I said to myself, I'm going to prove you wrong. And I said, how much do you make?
quotes.quote: I said to myself, I'm going to prove you wrong. And I said, how much do you make? And he said, that doesn't matter. And I said, it does to me. So that message stayed with me for a while in regards to that. And so I didn't play much as a freshman, but I didn't quit. I stayed, I worked, and I eventually became the school's all-time leading scorer and rebounder.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson on his NBA career and proving doubters wrong
quotes.excerpt: And when I made the NBA, I went looking for that TA. I did not find him.
quotes.quote: And when I made the NBA, I went looking for that TA. I did not find him. But I did not accept anybody's early evaluation of me and what I could not accomplish. I wouldn't have had the career I had. And that's why this conversation matters to me. Because whether we're discussing historical exclusion or modern sports analysis, there's a question worth asking. Who gets to decide what another human being is capable of achieving?

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson on the Chicago Bears and Draymond Green
quotes.excerpt: I woke up Sunday morning fired up by my Chicago Bears, coming off the bye week. By Sunday
quotes.quote: I woke up Sunday morning fired up by my Chicago Bears, coming off the bye week. By Sunday night, I'm watching Draymond Green talk about me at his press conference, because he made a good stop on Jason Tatum, but he still had the triple-double. How do we get here?

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson addresses a tweet about Hall of Fame credentials
quotes.excerpt: It started with this tweet. Name me a Potential Hall of Fame player that will have that
quotes.quote: It started with this tweet. Name me a Potential Hall of Fame player that will have that statistical personal Resume going into the Hall. Then you have players like Mark Aguirre, Tom Chambers, Shawn Marion, and Kevin Johnson not get in. I'm minding my own business. I have a right as an analyst. I have a national radio show, okay? Right for Hoops Hype. I have a right to say my opinion. Draymond came back hard, like he does when he takes something as a shot at him, a personal shot.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson on his NBA career and playoff appearances
quotes.excerpt: When I retired from the NBA, and you're right Draymond, a conference final doesn't mean anything to you.
quotes.quote: When I retired from the NBA, and you're right Draymond, a conference final doesn't mean anything to you, okay? That's what you told me in one of your tweets. Fine. But it meant something to me. It meant that I had a I was a step away from having a chance to get to a finals. And I got there four times. Unfortunately for me, this is what we played. Our first time we went, as a Phoenix Sun, we played the Lakers. Magic, Kareem, Worthy, they swept us.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson on his playoff experiences with the Suns and Sonics
quotes.excerpt: The second time I went, the following year with the Suns, Portland beat us. And if you remember
quotes.quote: The second time I went, the following year with the Suns, Portland beat us. And if you remember that Portland team, you know, they had Clyde Drexler, Kevin Duckworth, Buck Williams, Jerome Kersey, man I miss Jerome Kersey so much, and I miss Duckworth so much. Terry Porter. The third time I went, I went actually as a member of the Seattle SuperSonics. And we took the Suns to seven games, and Charles, that was his MVP year, they beat us.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson on his time in Greece and winning a championship
quotes.excerpt: So I guess I got one championship. And don't belittle it, because my Greek friends follow me on
quotes.quote: So I guess I got one championship. And don't belittle it, because my Greek friends follow me on Twitter and they'll come after you and then you're going to be mad at them. All right? So don't do it, because they back me up. That's like my beehive. All right? So look, I believe that Draymond will get into the Hall of Fame. Now, do I believe it's deserving? No, my opinion. My opinion. Not hating, a lot of guys I say I don't think should have gotten in. But I believe there's four guys that I mentioned in that tweet that have stronger cases.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson discusses Mark Aguirre's career and impact
quotes.excerpt: Let's start with Mark Aguirre. Mark Aguirre is my high school teammate. We called him Jaws.
quotes.quote: Let's start with Mark Aguirre. Mark Aguirre is my high school teammate. We called him Jaws. And let me tell you a little bit something about Jaws. He's the number one pick in the draft, okay? And then my other childhood friend, who you know, Isaiah Thomas was number two. But Mark was number one. And it was no shock to anybody, including Isaiah. Mark at that time, you know, high school kids weren't going to the NBA, but Mark was ready to go. He was ready to go to the NBA, without a doubt he was. Unbelievable. And when I mean unbelievable, he had everything, okay? Everything. Draymond, listen. Now, we can get people that can remark on this thing after, okay? They can. He would have worked you over, man. I'm telling you. And that's my belief. And I bust up a lot of great defenders. A lot of them. Go ask. Go. Ask Scotty was our nightmare to guard. Now, Scotty would lock my butt up a lot, because he can put them big hands on me. You know, we had, you know, he can just put them on my hip because he can hand check. Then it's Rodman. But I had my good games against them, dude. They knew when I showed up that they were going to have to work.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson defends his critique of Draymond Green's performance
quotes.excerpt: I honestly believe he would have won the championship in Phoenix, obviously, if Robert Horry didn't hip-check Steve Nash
quotes.quote: If you're thinking that I'm just saying stuff to say stuff, no, man. I do my homework. I honestly believe he would have won the championship in Phoenix, obviously, if Robert Horry didn't hip-check Steve Nash and Robert Horry is my boy. Didn't hip-check Steve Nash and cost us a championship. You know, I was the TV guy, though. I wasn't on the team, but I would have got a ring. I would have got my first ring.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson praises Kevin Johnson's career and impact
quotes.excerpt: He made four All-Star games, All-NBA twice, and as I told you, 2011, I think one of the best championships
quotes.quote: He made four All-Star games, All-NBA twice, and as I told you, 2011, I think one of the best championships any team, any group could ever have. They beat a Heat team that said not one, not two, not three, not four. So yeah, he should be. Best second jump, probably in history of the game. I don't think anybody, guys that probably jump higher than him, but they didn't have a second jump like he did.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson reflects on Kevin Johnson's stubbornness and career
quotes.excerpt: Kevin Johnson's career was cut short because he was stubborn, he wouldn't stretch
quotes.quote: Kevin Johnson's career was cut short because he was stubborn, he wouldn't stretch. He used to laugh at me all the time. Oh, old man, you stretching. And at that time, I was only 27 years old. But the reason I was able to play 18 years professionally is Draymond, I stretched. That's all, stretched. Played till I was 40. And Kevin's career got cut short, but it didn't matter. I mean, what he did, he was unguardable.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson suggests Magic Johnson as a source for his opinions
quotes.excerpt: Go talk to Magic. Magic and I are good friends. Go talk to Magic. Ask him how good Kevin Johnson was
quotes.quote: Go talk to Magic. Magic and I are good friends. Go talk to Magic. Ask him how good Kevin Johnson was. You hang out in LA, talk to Byron Scott, talk to Michael Cooper, talk to Kareem, if you're able to get to, to Kareem. They'll tell you how good he was. Unstoppable. Find me a guy 6'1 back in the 80s that dunked on two of the toughest guys in the history of the league to dunk on. Mark Eaton, and if you ever stood next to Mark Eaton, I'm telling, I guarantee you wouldn't have never kicked Mark Eaton. I guarantee you wouldn't have.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson highlights Mark Eaton's defensive dominance
quotes.excerpt: Mark Eaton, the number one shot blocking in history of the game. Dunked on him
quotes.quote: Mark Eaton, the number one shot blocking in history of the game. Dunked on him. So, jumper, left, right hand, pick your poison, didn't matter. Strong. I was, as a matter of fact, I was with Kevin last night. He gave a great speech. Washington Carver Museum in Phoenix, honoring the oldest high school in Arizona. It was nice. KJ, he's my boy. Deserves to be in.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson discusses Kevin Johnson's Hall of Fame credentials
quotes.excerpt: Kevin made three, he made five All-NBA teams, four second team, one third team
quotes.quote: Kevin made three, he made five All-NBA teams, four second team, one third team. He won most improved player the same year in '89, I won sixth man of the year. And then five times voter said he's one of the best guards in the league. That just tells you how good KJ was. Should be in the Hall of Fame before you, because he did more. He just didn't do one way, he did multiple ways.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson addresses critics of his social media takes
quotes.excerpt: When I tweeted that out, some people might look at it and they're going to break it down
quotes.quote: When I tweeted that out, some people might look at it and they're going to break it down, because you got a lot of people out there that, you know, a lot of people out there, they just going to say what they're going to say. Right? They're just going to say what they're going to say. But there's a lot of people out there that don't understand how good he is. Those four guys, I'm saying in the tweet, which is my opinion. I am an analyst. I've been an analyst, Draymond, if you don't know, I'll edify you on that one, too, because in your press conference, you were trying to make it seem like I got a $100 microphone and, uh, you know, they give anybody this and that. You just got into this business, man.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson explains his career longevity and expertise
quotes.excerpt: You're able to elevate yourself because why? You won some titles. That's what, that's what national TV does
quotes.quote: You're able to elevate yourself because why? You won some titles. That's what, that's what national TV does. That doesn't mean you're better. It just means that you're in a good position. That's all. Good for you. Good for you. But you're not more knowledgeable than me about this game. You're just not. That's my opinion. You can have your opinion, I'm going to have mine. You're not. But just so you know, been doing this, man, for 28 years since I retired. 28. You're doing it as a part-time gig. Part-time. We're going to find out. I hope Charles retires. I swear, I hope he retires. I hope they put you in his place, and I want to see how it works.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson challenges Draymond Green to a career comparison
quotes.excerpt: I'm not saying you're going to fail. I'm just saying, just know it's not as easy as you think
quotes.quote: I'm not saying you're going to fail. I'm just saying, just know it's not as easy as you think it is. That's all. You're just doing a little podcast and you're going there, you're talking about people and you're breaking people down, telling them what they can and can't do and all this stuff, and yet you struggle, but you're not telling us what's going on with you. I was one of them dudes. I say I stink. I say, man, I'm I stink. Really, I'll say it. It didn't matter, because you know why? Because I knew I was confident enough to turn it around. Didn't matter. See, so that's how you work. I'm not working that way. I'm just going to try to edify people, man. That's all I'm going to do.

quotes.speaker: Eddie Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Eddie Johnson concludes his response to Draymond Green
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to finish with you. I think that's fair. Right? It's fair
quotes.quote: I'm going to finish with you. I think that's fair. Right? It's fair. I'm going to give you your due. 2015-16, I think probably is your best year, right? You averaged 14 points, almost 10 rebounds, and seven and a half assists. And what I'm impressed with more is you're an Iron Man that year, 81 games. You made first team All-Defense. Right? But, you know, you were never consistent in scoring. Look, I'm not knocking your scoring. I call games, which you at Michigan State, all right? So I, I had a little ability to score, but something happened. So, you know, your career averages of nine points a game and six rebounds, five assists, it, it just doesn't jump out like Hall of Fame like, you know, numbers.
